enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Grading.GradingBlendMode` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

How a control behaves when a preset is blended toward the game's own look.

<a id="gradingcatalog"></a>

## `GradingCatalog`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Grading.GradingCatalog` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The presets the game knows: the player's own (`BepInEx/data/grading/`) and every loaded pack's `grading/*.json`. Resolves what `grade apply <name>` means.

A plain name (`warm-film`) picks the player's own preset of that name if there is one, otherwise the pack preset from the pack loaded last (the usual "later pack wins" rule); the lookup says which others it shadowed. A qualified name (`cwy.demo.scenery:warm-film`, `user:mine`) picks exactly that file. Case-insensitive throughout.

<a id="gradingcatalog--ctor"></a>

### `GradingCatalog(IEnumerable<GradingCatalogEntry> entries)`

Builds a catalogue.

**Parameters**

- `entries`: Every preset file found; null means none. Duplicate qualified names keep the last.

<a id="gradingcatalog--empty"></a>

### `static GradingCatalog Empty { get; }`

An empty catalogue.

<a id="gradingcatalog--entries"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<GradingCatalogEntry> Entries { get; }`

Every entry: user presets first, then packs in load order. Never null.

<a id="gradingcatalog--find"></a>

### `GradingCatalogEntry Find(string name, out IReadOnlyList<GradingCatalogEntry> shadowed)`

Finds the preset a name means.

**Parameters**

- `name`: A plain or qualified name; a trailing `.json` is ignored.
- `shadowed`: The other entries with the same plain name that lost; empty when none.

**Returns:** The entry, or null when nothing matches.

<a id="gradingcontrols"></a>

## `GradingControls`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Grading.GradingControls` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Every slider a grading preset can set, in Lightroom's panel order. A control's id is its JSON path in `grading/<name>.json` (`basic.exposure`, `hsl.blues.luminance`, `effects.vignette.amount`), and the name `grade set` accepts besides a short alias (`exposure`, `blues.luminance`).

Ranges follow Lightroom where the mapping allows: -100..100 for most sliders, -5..5 EV for exposure, 0..360 degrees for hues, 0..100 for saturations of tints. What each one maps to on the URP side is [`GradingMapper`](#gradingmapper)'s business and is tabled in `src/CwyLs.ModLoader.Bulbul/Grading/README.md`.

<a id="gradingcontrols--blend"></a>

### `const string Blend = "blend"`

Id of the blend weight (0..1).

<a id="gradingcontrols--degreesunit"></a>

### `const string DegreesUnit = "deg"`

Unit string of a hue angle; such a control wraps instead of clamping.

<a id="gradingcontrols--evunit"></a>

### `const string EvUnit = "EV"`

Unit string of an exposure value.

<a id="gradingcontrols--all"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<GradingControl> All { get; }`

Every control, in Lightroom's panel order. Never null.

<a id="gradingcontrols--grouppaths"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyCollection<string> GroupPaths { get; }`

Every group path a control id passes through (`basic`, `hsl`, `hsl.reds`, `effects.vignette` ...). The parser recurses into exactly these objects.

### `static IReadOnlyList<string> HslBands { get; }`

The eight HSL colour bands, in Lightroom's order.

<a id="gradingcontrols--hslproperties"></a>

<a id="gradingmapper"></a>

## `GradingMapper`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Grading.GradingMapper` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Maps a flat, blended preset (Lightroom units) onto URP volume overrides - the one place the numbers that decide how a preset looks are written down. Every constant below is a tuning choice, documented with its effect, and tabled in `src/CwyLs.ModLoader.Bulbul/Grading/README.md`.

Only components the game's own profiles do not use are overridden (the game's `Volume_{day,sunset,night,cloud}` hold Beautify + LiftGammaGain only), so the preset sits on top of the time-of-day look instead of replacing it. The one exception, bloom, is expressed as a factor on the game's own Beautify bloom for the same reason.

<a id="gradingmapper--contrastscale"></a>

### `const double ContrastScale = 0.5`

URP contrast per Lightroom contrast: +100 = URP +50 (log-space slope x1.5 around mid grey).

<a id="gradingmapper--darkenscale"></a>

### `const double DarkenScale = 0.5`

Luminance offset per -100 of a darkening slider: x0.5 linear (-1 stop) in that range.

<a id="gradingmapper--defaulthighlightsstart"></a>

### `const double DefaultHighlightsStart = 0.55`

URP's default start of the highlight range.

<a id="gradingmapper--defaultshadowsend"></a>

### `const double DefaultShadowsEnd = 0.3`

URP's default end of the shadow range.

<a id="gradingmapper--grainresponse"></a>

### `const double GrainResponse = 0.8`

URP film grain response (how much grain fades in bright areas); URP's default.

<a id="gradingmapper--graintypes"></a>

### `const int GrainTypes = 10`

How many grain textures URP ships (FilmGrainLookup Thin1..Large02).

<a id="gradingmapper--liftscale"></a>

### `const double LiftScale = 0.25`

Luminance offset (URP SMH `w`) per +100 of a lightening slider: x2 linear (+1 stop) in that range.

<a id="gradingmapper--vignettelighten"></a>

### `const double VignetteLighten = 0.6`

Edge brightness of a vignette at amount +100 (x1.6).

<a id="gradingmapper--wheelsaturationscale"></a>

### `const double WheelSaturationScale = 0.35`

How strongly a colour-grading wheel at saturation 100 tints its range (0..1 mix toward the pure hue).

<a id="gradingmapper--graintype"></a>

### `static int GrainType(double size)`

The film-grain texture index (Thin1 = 0 .. Large02 = 9) for a Lightroom grain size.

**Parameters**

- `size`: 0..100.

<a id="gradingmapper--luminanceoffset"></a>

### `static double LuminanceOffset(double slider)`

A luminance offset for URP's SMH `w`: + lightens (x2 linear at +100), - darkens (x0.5 at -100). URP applies `w * (w < 0 ? 1 : 4)` to the linear multiplier.

**Parameters**

- `slider`: -100..100.

<a id="gradingmapper--map"></a>

### `static GradingPlan Map(GradingPreset preset)`

Maps a flat preset. Resolve the time of day and apply the blend first.

**Parameters**

- `preset`: The preset in force (see [`GradingPreset.Resolve`](#gradingpreset--resolve) and [`GradingPreset.ApplyBlend`](#gradingpreset--applyblend)).

**Returns:** The plan; empty when the preset changes nothing.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `preset` is null.

<a id="gradingmapper--splittint"></a>

### `static Rgb SplitTint(double hue, double saturation)`

A split-toning tint: HSL(hue, saturation, 0.5) in gamma space, so saturation 0 is the neutral grey (0.5, 0.5, 0.5) URP's soft-light expects.

**Parameters**

- `hue`: 0..360.
- `saturation`: 0..100.

<a id="gradingmapper--wheelmultiplier"></a>

### `static Rgb WheelMultiplier(double hue, double saturation)`

A colour-grading wheel as a linear per-channel multiplier: the pure hue normalised by its mean, mixed in by `saturation / 100 *`[`GradingMapper.WheelSaturationScale`](#gradingmapper--wheelsaturationscale). (1, 1, 1) at saturation 0.

**Parameters**

- `hue`: 0..360.
- `saturation`: 0..100.

## `GradingPreset`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Grading.GradingPreset` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

A grading preset: the Lightroom-style slider values, tone curves and LUT file of one `grading/<name>.json`, plus the optional per-time-of-day blocks (`day`, `sunset`, `night`, `cloudy`) that override it while the game shows that look.

Immutable: every change returns a new preset, so the value a console command is editing and the value being rendered can never be half-updated. Only controls that were set are stored; an absent control means "leave the game alone", which is different from a control set to its neutral value only in that it is not written back by [`GradingPresetWriter`](#gradingpresetwriter).

The tone curves that were set. Never null.

A preset that sets nothing: the game's own look.

<a id="gradingpreset--values"></a>

### `IReadOnlyDictionary<string, double> Values { get; }`

The controls that were set, by canonical id. Never null.

<a id="gradingpreset--applyblend"></a>

### `GradingPreset ApplyBlend()`

This flat preset at its own `blend` weight: every strength control, curve and the LUT amount moved that far from the game's look toward the preset. The result has `blend` removed (it is now baked in) and no blocks.

Done here rather than with the URP volume's own weight because URP does not interpolate curves, LUT textures, enums or switches: a volume at weight 0.5 would apply the tone curve, the LUT and the grain type at full strength. Blending the sliders blends everything.

<a id="gradingpreset--curve"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<GradingCurvePoint> Curve(GradingCurveChannel channel)`

The points of one curve, or null when it was not set.

**Parameters**

- `channel`: The channel.

<a id="gradingpreset--get"></a>

### `double Get(string id)`

A control's value, or its neutral value when it was not set.

**Parameters**

- `id`: Canonical id.

**Exceptions**

- `KeyNotFoundException`: No control has that id.

<a id="gradingpreset--has"></a>

### `bool Has(string id)`

True when the control was set (to any value, neutral included).

**Parameters**

- `id`: Canonical id.

<a id="gradingpreset--lerp"></a>

### `static GradingPreset Lerp(GradingPreset from, GradingPreset to, double t)`

Interpolates two flat presets. A strength control goes from its value in `from` (neutral when unset) to its value in `to`; a shape control (hue angle, vignette midpoint, grain size) takes `to`'s value when `to` sets it, else `from`'s; hue angles take the shorter way round when both set them. Curves are sampled and blended; the LUT amount blends and the LUT file is `to`'s when `t > 0`.

**Parameters**

- `from`: Start; blocks are ignored.
- `to`: End; blocks are ignored.
- `t`: 0 = `from`, 1 = `to`; clamped.

<a id="gradingpreset--overlay"></a>

### `static GradingPreset Overlay(GradingPreset bottom, GradingPreset top)`

`top` laid over `bottom`: every control, curve channel and LUT file `top` sets wins. Name and blocks come from `bottom`.

**Parameters**

- `bottom`: The base.
- `top`: What overrides it.

<a id="gradingpreset--resolve"></a>

### `GradingPreset Resolve(GradingTimeOfDay timeOfDay)`

The flat preset in force while `timeOfDay` is the game's look: this preset with the matching block laid over it (a control, a curve channel or the LUT file the block sets replaces the base one). Without a matching block, the base alone. The result has no blocks.

**Parameters**

- `timeOfDay`: The game's current look.

True when both presets set the same things to the same values (within 1e-6).

**Parameters**

- `other`: The other preset.

<a id="gradingpresetparser"></a>

## `GradingPresetParser`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Grading.GradingPresetParser` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Reads a `grading/<name>.json` preset (schema [`GradingPreset.CurrentSchema`](#gradingpreset--currentschema)).

Lenient where a typo should not cost the look, strict where the file would be misread: malformed JSON, a root that is not an object and a schema newer than this build are fatal; an unknown member, a value out of range (clamped), a Lightroom setting with no faithful mapping and a missing `schema` (read as 1) are warnings; a value of the wrong type or a broken curve is an error that costs only that member. Members whose name starts with `x-` belong to the author and are skipped in silence.

<a id="gradingpresetparser--lutkey"></a>

<a id="gradingpresetparser--namekey"></a>

### `const string NameKey = "name"`

<a id="gradingtimeofday"></a>

## `GradingTimeOfDay`

enum · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Grading.GradingTimeOfDay` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

The game's own time-of-day looks, as far as a grading preset is concerned.

The game switches its look with `Bulbul.WindowViewService.ChangeWeatherAndTime` (game 1.17.3), which turns one of four objects on - `Paremt/EnviromentObject/DateTime/{day,sunset,night,Cloudy}` in `RoomScene`, each carrying a global `Volume` with its own Beautify + LiftGammaGain profile (`Volume_day`, `Volume_sunset`, `Volume_night`, `Volume_cloud`) - and publishes the choice as `WindowViewService.CurrentTimeOfDayType` (`Bulbul.WindowTimeOfDayType`: Day = 11, Sunset, Night, Cloudy).

| Name | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="gradingtimeofday--unknown"></a>`Unknown` | 0 | Not known yet (before the room is up), or a value this build does not recognise. |
| <a id="gradingtimeofday--day"></a>`Day` | 1 | `WindowTimeOfDayType.Day`. |

<a id="gradingtonecurves"></a>

## `GradingToneCurves`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Grading.GradingToneCurves` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Turns Lightroom-style tone controls into the keys of URP `ColorCurves`.

**The domain is the trap.** Lightroom's curve takes display values (0..255, gamma encoded). URP's HDR LUT builder (this game grades in HDR: `m_ColorGradingMode: 1` in every `PC_URP-*.asset`) evaluates the YRGB curves on `FastTonemap(linear)` = `c / (1 + max(r, g, b))`, so display white (linear 1) sits at curve input 0.5 and the upper half of the curve is HDR headroom. A Lightroom point (x, y) is therefore placed at ([`GradingToneCurves.ToCurveSpace`](#gradingtonecurves--tocurvespace)(x), [`GradingToneCurves.ToCurveSpace`](#gradingtonecurves--tocurvespace)(y)), and a key at (1, 1) keeps the headroom an identity. Exact for greys; for saturated colours the shared denominator makes it an approximation.

<a id="gradingtonecurves--levelsrange"></a>

### `const double LevelsRange = 0.15`

How far `basic.blacks`/`basic.whites` at +/-100 move the black or white point, in display units (0.15 = 38 of 255).

<a id="gradingtonecurves--samples"></a>

### `const int Samples = 17`

How many evenly spaced display values a composed curve is sampled at (plus its own knots).

<a id="gradingtonecurves--vibranceboost"></a>

### `const double VibranceBoost = 0.6`

Vibrance +100 multiplies the saturation of a grey-ish colour by 1 + this.

<a id="gradingtonecurves--vibrancecut"></a>

### `const double VibranceCut = 0.8`

Vibrance -100 multiplies the saturation of a grey-ish colour by 1 - this.

<a id="gradingtonecurves--channel"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<CurveKey> Channel(IReadOnlyList<GradingCurvePoint> points)`

One of the red/green/blue point curves, mapped into URP's curve space; null when unset or an identity.

**Parameters**

- `points`: The channel's points.

<a id="gradingtonecurves--levels"></a>

### `static void Levels(double blacks, double whites, out double x0, out double y0, out double x1, out double y1)`

The levels implied by blacks and whites: input x0..x1 maps to output y0..y1.

**Parameters**

- `blacks`: -100..100.
- `whites`: -100..100.
- `x0`: Input black point.
- `y0`: Output black point.
- `x1`: Input white point.
- `y1`: Output white point.

<a id="gradingtonecurves--master"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<CurveKey> Master(GradingPreset preset)`

The master curve: `basic.blacks` and `basic.whites` as levels, then the `toneCurve.master` points, composed and mapped into URP's curve space. Null when both are neutral.

**Parameters**

- `preset`: A flat, blended preset.

<a id="gradingtonecurves--tocurvespace"></a>

### `static double ToCurveSpace(double display)`

A display value (0..1, sRGB-encoded) as URP's curve input: linearise, then `L / (1 + L)`. 0 maps to 0, display white to 0.5.

**Parameters**

- `display`: Display value.

<a id="gradingtonecurves--vibrance"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<CurveKey> Vibrance(double vibrance)`

The `satVsSat` curve for `presence.vibrance`: a saturation multiplier that is largest for greyish colours and fades to 1 for fully saturated ones; stored halved (URP multiplies the curve value by 2). Null at 0.

**Parameters**

- `vibrance`: -100..100.

<a id="hsladjustment"></a>

## `HslAdjustment`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Grading.HslAdjustment` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

Lightroom's HSL / colour mixer: hue, saturation and luminance for eight colour bands, as a pure function on display (sRGB-encoded) colours. It is baked into the LUT that URP's `ColorLookup` applies (URP's `ColorCurves` has hue-vs-hue and hue-vs-saturation but no hue-vs-luminance, so one baked function keeps the three consistent).

Band centres (degrees): reds 0, oranges 30, yellows 60, greens 120, aquas 180, blues 240, purples 270, magentas 300. Between two neighbouring centres the weights cross-fade with a smoothstep, so the weights always sum to 1 and a colour halfway between orange and yellow gets half of each band's adjustment.

- Hue -100..100 turns the band up to [`HslAdjustment.MaxHueShiftDegrees`](#hsladjustment--maxhueshiftdegrees) toward its neighbour (reds +100 toward orange).
- Saturation -100..100 multiplies HSV saturation by 0..2.
- Luminance -100..100 scales the linear colour by 1 -/+ [`HslAdjustment.LuminanceScale`](#hsladjustment--luminancescale), weighted by the colour's saturation so greys never move.

<a id="hsladjustment--ctor"></a>

### `HslAdjustment(double[] hue, double[] saturation, double[] luminance)`

Creates an adjustment from per-band values (-100..100 each), in band order.

**Parameters**

- `hue`: Eight hue values.
- `saturation`: Eight saturation values.
- `luminance`: Eight luminance values.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: An array does not have eight entries.

<a id="hsladjustment--luminancescale"></a>

### `const double LuminanceScale = 0.6`

The linear brightness change of a fully saturated colour at luminance +/-100.

<a id="hsladjustment--maxhueshiftdegrees"></a>

### `const double MaxHueShiftDegrees = 30.0`

The largest hue turn of a band at +/-100, in degrees.

<a id="hsladjustment--saturationknee"></a>

### `const double SaturationKnee = 0.25`

Below this HSV saturation a colour counts as grey for luminance (full effect from here up).

<a id="hsladjustment--bandcenters"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<double> BandCenters { get; }`

Band centres in degrees, in [`GradingControls.HslBands`](#gradingcontrols--hslbands) order.

<a id="hsladjustment--apply"></a>

### `Rgb Apply(Rgb srgb)`

Applies the adjustment to one display (sRGB-encoded, 0..1) colour.

**Parameters**

- `srgb`: The colour.

**Returns:** The adjusted colour, clamped to 0..1.

<a id="hsladjustment--cachekey"></a>

### `string CacheKey()`

A stable key for caching a baked LUT: the 24 values, invariant.

<a id="hsladjustment--frompreset"></a>

### `static HslAdjustment FromPreset(GradingPreset preset)`

The HSL part of a flat preset, or null when every band is neutral.

**Parameters**

- `preset`: A flat (resolved, blended) preset.

<a id="hsladjustment--weights"></a>

### `static void Weights(double hueDegrees, double[] weights)`

The weight of each band at a hue: two neighbouring bands share it with a smoothstep cross-fade, so the weights are non-negative and sum to exactly 1.

**Parameters**

- `hueDegrees`: Any hue; wrapped.
- `weights`: Receives eight weights.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: `weights` is shorter than eight.

<a id="lut3d"></a>

## `Lut3D`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Grading.Lut3D` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

A 3D colour lookup table: `Size`^3 RGB entries over the unit cube, red varying fastest (the `.cube` order). Pure data with trilinear sampling, `.cube` parsing, and the conversions to and from the horizontal strip layout URP's `ColorLookup` samples.

Strip layout (URP `ApplyLut2D`): width = N x N, height = N; the texel at `x = r + N * b`, `y = g` (y = 0 is the bottom row, Unity's texture convention) holds the output for input `(r, g, b) / (N - 1)`. Inputs and outputs are sRGB-encoded: URP converts to sRGB before the lookup and back after it.

<a id="lut3d--maxsize"></a>

### `const int MaxSize = 65`

Largest size accepted (65 is the largest common `.cube` size).

<a id="lut3d--minsize"></a>

### `const int MinSize = 2`

Smallest size accepted.

<a id="lut3d--size"></a>

### `int Size { get; }`

Entries per axis.

<a id="lut3d--at"></a>

### `Rgb At(int r, int g, int b)`

The output stored at a grid point.

**Parameters**

- `r`: Red index.
- `g`: Green index.
- `b`: Blue index.

<a id="lut3d--bake"></a>

### `static Lut3D Bake(int size, Func<Rgb, Rgb> transform)`

Builds a table by evaluating `transform` at every grid point.

**Parameters**

- `size`: Entries per axis.
- `transform`: The colour function, on 0..1 sRGB-encoded colours.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The size is outside [`Lut3D.MinSize`](#lut3d--minsize)..[`Lut3D.MaxSize`](#lut3d--maxsize).
- `ArgumentNullException`: `transform` is null.

<a id="lut3d--fromstrip"></a>

### `static Lut3D FromStrip(int width, int height, IReadOnlyList<float> rgba, out string problem)`

Reads a strip image back into a table (the inverse of [`Lut3D.ToStripRgba`](#lut3d--tostriprgba)).

**Parameters**

- `width`: Image width; must be height squared.
- `height`: Image height = entries per axis.
- `rgba`: Pixels, RGBA, row by row from the bottom row up (Unity's `GetPixels` order).
- `problem`: Why the image is not a strip LUT, or null.

**Returns:** The table, or null.

<a id="lut3d--identity"></a>

### `static Lut3D Identity(int size)`

The identity table: every entry is its own input.

**Parameters**

- `size`: Entries per axis.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`: The size is outside [`Lut3D.MinSize`](#lut3d--minsize)..[`Lut3D.MaxSize`](#lut3d--maxsize).

<a id="lut3d--parsecube"></a>

### `static Lut3D ParseCube(string text, out string problem)`

Parses an Adobe/Resolve `.cube` file: `LUT_3D_SIZE`, optional `TITLE`/`DOMAIN_MIN`/`DOMAIN_MAX`, `#` comments, then size^3 lines of three numbers with red varying fastest. A non-default domain is folded in by resampling.

**Parameters**

- `text`: The whole file.
- `problem`: Why the file was refused, or null.

**Returns:** The table, or null.

<a id="lut3d--sample"></a>

### `Rgb Sample(Rgb input)`

Trilinear lookup; the input is clamped to the unit cube.

**Parameters**

- `input`: An sRGB-encoded colour.

<a id="lut3d--tostriprgba"></a>

### `float[] ToStripRgba()`

The table as a strip texture's pixels: RGBA floats, row by row from the bottom row up, width = N x N, height = N, alpha 1.

<a id="monotonecubic"></a>

## `MonotoneCubic`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Grading.MonotoneCubic` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader.Core`

A piecewise cubic Hermite spline through a set of points with Fritsch-Carlson tangents: it never overshoots between two points, so a tone curve drawn through monotone points stays monotone (no ringing, no inverted tones), and a local extremum gets a flat tangent.

The tangents are exactly what Unity's `Keyframe(time, value, inTangent, outTangent)` wants - an `AnimationCurve` evaluates a segment as the same cubic Hermite - so the curve the game samples is the curve tested here.

<a id="monotonecubic--ctor"></a>

### `MonotoneCubic(double[] xs, double[] ys)`

Builds the spline.

**Parameters**

- `xs`: Strictly increasing inputs.
- `ys`: Outputs, same length as `xs`.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: The arrays are empty, of different lengths, or the inputs are not strictly increasing.

<a id="monotonecubic--count"></a>

### `int Count { get; }`

How many points the spline passes through.

<a id="monotonecubic--evaluate"></a>

### `double Evaluate(double x)`

The spline at `x`; flat (the end value) outside the points.

**Parameters**

- `x`: Input.

<a id="monotonecubic--tangent"></a>

### `double Tangent(int i)`

Slope at point `i` (the Keyframe's in- and out-tangent).

**Parameters**

- `i`: Point index.

<a id="monotonecubic--x"></a>

### `double X(int i)`

Input of point `i`.

**Parameters**

- `i`: Point index.

<a id="monotonecubic--y"></a>

### `double Y(int i)`

Output of point `i`.

**Parameters**

- `i`: Point index.
